stories.title: Does Satoshi Nakamoto Really Hold 1.1 Million Bitcoin?
stories.summary: A Cointelegraph feature re-examines the long-held claim that Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator controls about 1.1 million BTC in dormant early wallets. The piece questions how solid the evidence for that widely cited figure really is. No new wallet movement or disclosure is reported.
stories.whyItMatters: The size and status of the 'Satoshi stash' is one of the biggest supply-side tail risks priced into Bitcoin, so doubts about the figure matter to long-term holders.
whatToWatch: Any new activity on wallets attributed to Satoshi
Follow-up analysis from on-chain researchers on the 1.1 million BTC estimate
questions: What evidence actually underpins the 1.1 million BTC figure?
Would a revised estimate change how the market prices Bitcoin's available supply?

sources.title: Big Questions: Does Satoshi actually own 1.1 million Bitcoin?

stories.title: Bitcoin Holds Near $86K as Oil Slide and Short Squeeze Fuel Bull Talk
stories.summary: Bitcoin pushed toward $86,000 and is trying to turn that level into support, a move that coincided with oil prices dropping below $90 a barrel. CryptoSlate reported about $1 billion in short positions liquidated as price cleared $86,000, with traders now eyeing $90,000 next. Cointelegraph noted some analysts are already calling this the start of a new bull market.
stories.whyItMatters: A break above $86,000 with large short liquidations points to forced buying, not just organic demand, which matters for judging how durable the move is.
whatToWatch: Whether $86K holds as support on a retest
Progress toward the $90K level traders are now watching
Further short liquidations if the price keeps climbing
questions: Is this rally driven by spot demand or by short covering?
How much is the oil price move actually influencing crypto, versus coincidence?

stories.title: Moscow Exchange Launches Five Crypto Perpetual Futures
stories.summary: Moscow Exchange has launched five crypto perpetual futures contracts, CryptoSlate reports, with demand reportedly topping 600 billion rubles. The launch gives Russian traders regulated, ruble-denominated derivatives exposure to major cryptocurrencies.
stories.whyItMatters: A major national exchange rolling out crypto derivatives shows growing institutional appetite for regulated crypto exposure in a market largely cut off from Western venues.
whatToWatch: Trading volumes on the new contracts in coming weeks
Whether other Russian exchanges follow with similar products
questions: How is the 600 billion ruble figure measured — pre-launch interest or actual trading volume?
Which assets do the five contracts track?

sources.title: Moscow Exchange launches 5 crypto perpetual futures as demand tops 600 billion rubles

stories.title: Zcash Gets Its First European ETP After US ETF Debut
stories.summary: Zcash has received its first European exchange-traded product, Cointelegraph reports, following the recent launch of a US Zcash ETF. The listing gives European investors regulated access to the privacy-focused cryptocurrency.
stories.whyItMatters: Regulated fund access to a privacy coin is notable given regulators' past wariness of privacy features, and it signals demand for exposure beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum.
whatToWatch: Early inflows into the European ETP
Whether other privacy coins get similar listings
questions: Which exchange and issuer are behind the European ETP?
Will European regulators apply extra scrutiny given Zcash's privacy features?

sources.title: Zcash gets first European ETP following US ETF launch

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs Absorb 11,500 BTC in Biggest Buying Day in Nearly Two Years
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about 11,500 BTC in a single day, CryptoSlate reports, the largest daily net purchase in almost two years. The surge lines up with Bitcoin's push back toward $86,000.
stories.whyItMatters: A buying day this large shows institutional demand through the ETF wrapper accelerating sharply, a key gauge of whether the current price move has real backing.
whatToWatch: Whether this pace of inflows continues in coming sessions
Issuer-level flow breakdowns for signs of concentration
questions: Which ETF issuers drove most of the buying?
Is this fresh capital or rotation from other crypto products?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs just absorbed 11,500 BTC in their biggest buying day in nearly two years

stories.title: Narrowing Price Cushions Leave Bitcoin-Backed Loans Exposed to 4.7% Dips
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that the price buffer protecting Bitcoin-collateralized loans has narrowed to the point that a 4.7% price drop could trigger liquidations. The report says Aave is weighing whether to allow higher leverage on these loans.
stories.whyItMatters: Thin liquidation cushions raise the risk of cascading forced selling on even a modest Bitcoin dip, which can amplify volatility across the wider market.
whatToWatch: Any Aave governance decision on raising leverage limits
Liquidation volumes if Bitcoin pulls back from current levels
questions: How concentrated are these thin-cushion positions among a few large borrowers?
Would higher leverage limits reduce the risk or just redistribute it?

sources.title: Narrowing price cushions leave Bitcoin loans vulnerable to 4.7% price dips as Aave weighs higher leverage

stories.title: ECB to Put Its Own Money Into Tokenized Securities via New Pontes DLT
stories.summary: The European Central Bank plans to invest its own funds into tokenized securities through a new distributed ledger platform called Pontes, Cointelegraph reports. It marks a direct financial commitment from the central bank to the tokenization infrastructure it is helping build.
stories.whyItMatters: A central bank backing tokenized securities infrastructure with its own balance sheet is a strong institutional signal for tokenization in European capital markets.
whatToWatch: Details on how much ECB capital goes into Pontes
Timeline for Pontes going live and which securities it will support
questions: How does Pontes relate to the ECB's existing wholesale DLT settlement trials?
Which other institutions will use the platform?

sources.title: ECB to put its own money into tokenized securities via new Pontes DLT

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs Take In Nearly $1B as Average Holder Returns to Profit
stories.summary: US Bitcoin ETFs pulled in close to $1 billion in a single day, Decrypt reports, as the average Bitcoin holder moved back into unrealized profit after the recent price recovery. The inflow adds to signs of renewed institutional buying.
stories.whyItMatters: The average holder returning to profit shrinks the pool of underwater sellers who might dump at breakeven, a dynamic that has weighed on past rallies.
whatToWatch: Whether ETF inflows keep pace in coming days
On-chain holder profitability as price moves
questions: How is the 'average holder' cost basis calculated, and how sensitive is it to a pullback?

sources.title: Bitcoin ETFs Take Nearly $1B in a Day as Average Holder Returns to Profit

stories.title: ECB and EU Central Banks Push for Changes to MiCA's Stablecoin Deposit Rule
stories.summary: The European Central Bank and other EU central banks are seeking changes to the minimum bank deposit requirement MiCA imposes on stablecoin issuers, Cointelegraph reports. The rule currently sets a fixed share of reserves that issuers must hold in bank deposits.
stories.whyItMatters: Changes to MiCA's reserve rules would directly affect how euro-denominated stablecoins are backed and could reshape competition among issuers in the EU.
whatToWatch: Formal proposals or amendments to MiCA's reserve requirements
Reaction from stablecoin issuers operating under MiCA
questions: What specific change to the deposit minimum are the central banks proposing?
Would the change loosen or tighten requirements on issuers?

sources.title: ECB, EU cenbanks seek changes in MiCA’s minimum bank deposit for stablecoins

stories.title: Large ETF Outflows Threaten Bitcoin's Fragile Push to $86,000
stories.summary: CryptoSlate warns that large capital exits from Bitcoin ETFs could undercut the cryptocurrency's recent climb to $86,000, calling the price surge fragile. The warning stands in contrast to same-day reports of record ETF buying.
stories.whyItMatters: Conflicting flow reports on the same day show how fast ETF-driven sentiment can flip, which matters for judging whether $86,000 is a durable floor.
whatToWatch: Net daily ETF flow data over the next few sessions to resolve the conflicting picture
Whether $86K holds if outflows materialize
questions: How does this outflow warning square with same-day reports of record ETF buying?
Which specific ETFs are seeing exits?

sources.title: Massive ETF capital exits threaten Bitcoin’s fragile $86,000 price surge

stories.title: White Hats Race Ahead of Coldcard Hackers to Save 52 Bitcoin
stories.summary: Cointelegraph reports that white-hat security researchers moved faster than attackers targeting Coldcard hardware wallet users, evacuating 52 BTC before hackers could steal it. The incident points to an active exploit or scam campaign aimed at Coldcard users.
stories.whyItMatters: An attack aimed at a widely used hardware wallet brand is a direct threat to self-custody, the practice crypto holders rely on to avoid exchange risk.
whatToWatch: Official disclosure from Coldcard on the vulnerability or scam vector used
Guidance for affected users to secure their wallets
questions: What was the actual attack vector — a software flaw, phishing, or supply-chain compromise?
How many other wallets were exposed but not rescued in time?

sources.title: White hats outrun Coldcard hackers in 52-Bitcoin evacuation

stories.title: Bitcoin Breaks Out as Nasdaq Hits Records and Oil Slides on Iran Hopes
stories.summary: Bitcoin rallied alongside a broader risk-on move, Decrypt reports, as the Nasdaq set fresh records and oil prices fell on hopes of easing tensions with Iran. The moves suggest crypto is trading in step with wider macro risk appetite rather than on crypto-specific catalysts.
stories.whyItMatters: When Bitcoin tracks equities and geopolitical risk instead of crypto-specific news, it signals the asset is currently trading as a macro risk asset, which changes what to watch for continuation or reversal.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitcoin keeps tracking equity market moves or decouples
Any shift in Iran tensions that could reverse the oil move
questions: Is this correlation with equities a durable shift or a short-term coincidence?

sources.title: Bitcoin Breaks Out as Nasdaq Hits Records and Oil Slides on Iran Hopes
